source_findings.claim: The transition begins with a large position jump from hang to the gathered orbit pose.
source_findings.evidence: Hang pelvis z is 1.205; orbit(0) pelvis z is BAR_Z - 0.50 = 1.80. Those poses are keyed at t=0.10 and 0.18, only 0.36 s apart in the 4.5 s clip.

source_findings.claim: The main orbit is a fast, sparse four-quarter rotation followed by a very fast reverse.
source_findings.evidence: Orbit angles 0/90/180/270/360 are reached at normalized times .18/.30/.40/.48/.58, then the reverse sequence runs from .81 to .995. The final four reverse quarter-turns are packed into 0.83 s, about 0.21 s per quarter-turn at a 4.5 s duration.

source_findings.claim: The move to support and the return from support each include a substantial pelvis-height change over a short interval.
source_findings.evidence: The orbit endpoint has pelvis z=1.80; support uses z=2.46. They are keyed at .58 and .66 (0.36 s apart), and support to orbit(360) occurs from .75 to .81 (0.27 s apart).

source_findings.claim: The source does not encode a distinct slow lowering from support through the same controlled phases.
source_findings.evidence: Support is held from .66 to .75, then the full reverse orbit is completed by .995; the catalog explicitly says to lower back down slowly.

source_findings.claim: The hand targets remain at hang height for the orbit and then shift for the support pose, while shoulder and trunk orientation make a full 360-degree turn.
source_findings.evidence: Orbit hands are built with _hands(z=HANG_Z, ...); support uses wrist z=BAR_Z+.06, palms reversed and hands rotated, with p1/p2 set to 360 for both endpoints.

old_encoded_frame_observations: The old contact sheet shows hang, bent-arm pull, near-horizontal/inverted-looking body, support-like poses, then another horizontal/inverted sample on the return. The order and spacing read as abrupt from these sparse stills.
The last sampled frame at 4.46 s appears bent-arm below the bar rather than matching the straight-arm opening hang exactly.
The bar visually overlaps or obscures the body in horizontal/inverted samples, so hand/hip contact cannot be judged from this camera and scale.
plausible_movement_phases: Begin in a quiet straight-arm hang with both hands fixed on the bar; initiate a deliberate pull before raising the hips.

Bring the knees and hips toward and over the bar in a compact, controlled path. Allow a brief tuck for clearance if needed, then extend through the rotation rather than snapping through four equal quarter-turns.
Keep the hips close to the bar as the shoulders and torso roll over the hands; arrive with the chest above the bar and settle into front support with hands still contacting the bar.
Pause briefly in a stable support, then lower slowly through the reversed path, controlling the hips and legs around the bar back to a full hang.
specific_review_checks: Inspect the initial pull to ensure the pelvis rises progressively from hang instead of jumping directly into a raised gathered pose.
Check several frames around the bottom-to-over-bar transition: hips should travel close to the bar, legs should clear it without clipping, and the hands should remain attached.
Check that the trunk rotation does not spin ahead of the hips/legs or accelerate abruptly at the 90/180/270-degree phase boundaries.
Check the arrival into front support for a smooth transfer of load from hanging to pressing, without a vertical pop or hands moving through the bar.
Check the full descent separately: it should take enough time to read as a controlled reverse, remain continuous through inversion, and finish in the same straight-arm hang used at the start.

Compare clip duration against the requested use; the inspected source sets 4.5 s, already longer than four seconds, but its active return is compressed into the last ~0.9 s. Judge perceived duration from the revised encode rather than duration metadata alone.
limitations: Old visual evidence is a contact sheet of selected encoded frames, not full playback; it cannot establish the exact duration, motion smoothness or contact continuity between samples.
The phase sequence above is a movement-review proposal, not a certified technique standard.

candidate_phase_review.evidence_type: Twelve actual Cycles phase frames sampled across an 11-second loop; this is selected rendered evidence, not full playback.
observations: The sampled ascent reads in a coherent sequence: straight hang at 0.00 s, chest-height pull at 1.33 s, torso/hips rotating toward and over the bar at 2.00–4.00 s, then upright front support by 4.83 s and a held support at 5.75 s.

The sampled return reverses through a long-body horizontal position at 6.83 s, an inverted position at 7.92 s, a bent-arm/angled hang at 9.33 s, and a straight hang at 10.96 s. These endpoints and broad phases look more coherent and controlled than the old sheet.

The body and legs appear extended during much of the orbit, with no obvious clipping or abrupt quarter-turn stop visible in these samples. A compact knee action is not apparent; the hips and extended legs travel around the bar as one long lever.
candidate_phase_review.owner_reported_geometry_and_timing: Root reports 3,965,808 of 3,965,808 actual body/hand vertices inside the app frame across 264 frames; minimum mesh/bar gap 4.689 mm; whole-finger capsule clearance 1.174 mm; source maximum joint speed 2.079 m/s versus old 32.64; maximum acceleration 5.969 versus old 729.8; return central duration 1.167 times ascent; and no quarter-turn stops. I did not independently reproduce these measurements.
material_concerns: Several inverted/horizontal poses place the torso close to the bar and the hands appear to remain planted, but the small side-angle overview does not clearly show exact palm and wrist contact through the rollover.

The catalog wording says to bring the knees and hips over the bar. The sampled path uses a mostly extended body; confirm that this deliberate long-lever version still reads clearly as a pullover and that the legs clear without a visible snap.
The front-support arrival is upright and visually legible, but still frames cannot establish the load transfer or continuity into and out of support.
candidate_phase_review.assessment: The selected phases support the candidate's improved broad movement order, extended transition over the bar, a visible support, and more balanced return. No material abruptness is evident in the sampled poses.
candidate_phase_review.uncertainty: Moderate for phase order and silhouettes; high for motion continuity, contact, and perceived smoothness between the 12 sampled frames.
